[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Callbacks and Custom Training Loops in TensorFlow"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"While Keras provides the convenient model.fit() API for standard training, advanced machine learning workflows often require fine-grained control over the training process. This tutorial covers how to implement custom training loops using GradientTape and how to write custom callbacks to monitor and modify training dynamics in TensorFlow."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, ensure you have TensorFlow installed and import the necessary modules. We will use TensorFlow and NumPy for this demonstration."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import tensorflow as tf
import numpy as np

print('TensorFlow version:', tf.__version__)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Writing a Custom Training Loop"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"To build a custom training loop, you need to manage the forward pass, loss calculation, gradient computation, and weight updates manually. TensorFlow makes this possible using tf.GradientTape."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Generate synthetic data
X = np.random.randn(1000, 32).astype(np.float32)
y = np.random.randint(0, 2, size=(1000, 1)).astype(np.float32)

dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((X, y)).batch(32)

# Define a simple model
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(16, activation='relu', input_shape=(32,)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
])

optimizer = tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=0.001)
loss_fn = tf.keras.losses.BinaryCrossentropy()"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, we write the training step function utilizing GradientTape and execute it over multiple epochs."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"@tf.function
def train_step(x_batch, y_batch):
    with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
        preds = model(x_batch, training=True)
        loss = loss_fn(y_batch, preds)
    grads = tape.gradient(loss, model.trainable_variables)
    optimizer.apply_gradients(zip(grads, model.trainable_variables))
    return loss

epochs = 3
for epoch in range(epochs):
    print('Epoch:', epoch + 1)
    for step, (x_batch, y_batch) in enumerate(dataset):
        loss_value = train_step(x_batch, y_batch)
        if step % 10 == 0:
            print('Step', step, 'Loss:', float(loss_value))"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating Custom Callbacks"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Callbacks are objects that can perform actions at various stages of training (e.g., at the start or end of a batch or epoch). You can create custom callbacks by inheriting from tf.keras.callbacks.Callback."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"class CustomCallback(tf.keras.callbacks.Callback):
    def on_epoch_begin(self, epoch, logs=None):
        print('Starting epoch:', epoch)

    def on_epoch_end(self, epoch, logs=None):
        print('Finished epoch:', epoch, 'Loss:', logs.get('loss'))"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can now pass your custom callback into the standard model.fit() function to execute it during training."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='binary_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])
model.fit(dataset, epochs=2, callbacks=[CustomCallback()])"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary and Best Practices"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use tf.GradientTape for custom training loops when you need non-standard gradient updates or custom loss calculations."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Decorate training step functions with @tf.function to leverage TensorFlow graph compilation for significant performance speedups."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement custom callbacks to handle logging, checkpointing, or dynamic learning rate adjustments tailored to your pipeline requirements."}]
